NONE: › written abbreviation for adverb
副詞（adverb的縮寫）

I or T: › [ I or T ] to go or move something forward, or to develop or improve something
（使）前進；使進步，使進展；使發展；促進

T: › [ T ] to pay someone some money before the regular time
› [ T ] formal to suggest an idea or theory

I: › [ I ] If something such as a share price advances, it increases in value.

C or U: B2 [ C or U ] the forward movement of something, or an improvement or development in something

NONE: › money paid to someone before the regular time
預付的款項

C usually plural: › [ C usually plural ] an attempt to start a sexual or romantic relationship with someone

C: › [ C ] something such as a share price that increases in value

NONE: › happening, done, or ready before an event
預先的，事先的

example: The fire advanced steadily through the forest.
大火在森林中不斷蔓延。
The troops advanced on the city (= approached it, ready to attack).
軍隊向該城推進。
We have advanced greatly in our knowledge of the universe.
在認識宇宙方面，我們已經取得長足的進步。
Her study has considerably advanced (= helped) the cause of equal rights.
她的研究極大地促進了權利平等運動的事業。
He's just trying to advance (= improve) his own career.
他只是在努力發展自己的事業。
[ + two objects ] Could you advance me £500 until Tuesday?
週二之前可以預付給我500英鎊嗎？
the theory advanced in this article
這篇論文提出的理論
Nothing could stop the advance of the floodwaters.
洪水滔滔而來，勢不可擋。
Recent advances in medical science mean that this illness can now be cured.
醫學新近取得的進展意味著這種疾病現在不再是絕症了。
She asked for a £300 advance on her salary.
她要求預付她300英鎊薪金。
She rejected his unwelcome advances.
她拒絕了他的勾引，讓他碰了一鼻子灰。
We got no advance warning/notice of the changes.
我們事先沒有得到有關變更的警告／通知。

NONE: › another term for
living will
B1 modern and well developed
先進的
A2 at a higher, more difficult level
高等的；高級的
› a school class that is doing work of a higher standard than is usual for students at that stage in their education
高級班／課程

example: This is the most advanced type of engine available.
這是現有的最先進的引擎。
an advanced English course
高級英語課程

NONE: › the development or improvement of something
發展，提高，改善

example: All she was interested in was the advancement of her own career.
她心中只想著如何發展自己的事業。

NONE: › If you talk about someone's advancing age, you mean that they are getting older.
年事已高

example: He only recently stopped working, due to his advancing years.
他直到最近才因年事已高停止工作。

C or U: B1 [ C or U ] a condition giving a greater chance of success
有利條件，有利因素；優勢；好處
B1 to use the good things in a situation
› to treat someone badly in order to get something good from them
U: › [ U ] the word used in tennis when a player has won the point after deuce
（網球中的）局末平分後佔先，優勢分
› In games such as football, if a referee plays advantage, they do not stop the game when there is a foul because allowing play to continue gives an advantage to the team that has been fouled.
（足球比賽中）裁判根據對被犯規方有利的原則允許比賽繼續進行

example: The advantage of booking tickets in advance is that you get better seats.
提前訂票的好處就是可以得到比較好的座位。
Despite the twin advantages of wealth and beauty, she did not have a happy life.
儘管擁有財富和美貌的雙重優勢，她的生活並不幸福。
[ + to infinitive ] It would be to your advantage (= it would improve the situation for you) to agree to his demands.
答應他的要求對你有利。
For a goalkeeper, it's a great advantage to have big hands.
對守門員來說，長一雙大手是很大的優勢。
His height and reach give him a big advantage over (= make him better than) other boxers.
他身高臂長，這使他在和其他拳擊手較量時佔有很大優勢。
UK formal "Do you know how old I am?" "I'm afraid you have the advantage of me there (= you know the answer but I do not)."
「你知道我多大了嗎？」「恐怕我不知道。」
I thought I'd take advantage of the sports facilities while I'm here.
我想趁我在這兒期間，好好利用一下這裡的體育設施。
I think she takes advantage of his good nature.
我認為她利用他善良的本性佔他的便宜。
I know she's offered to babysit, but I don't want her to think we're taking advantage of her.
我知道她主動提出來照顧我們的孩子，但是我不想讓她覺得我們在佔她的便宜。
Advantage Miss Williams!
威廉斯小姐佔先！
The ref should have played advantage because Rooney would have been through on goal.
裁判當時應該根據對被犯規方有利的原則允許比賽繼續進行，因為魯尼本來有可能進球的。

NONE: › giving advantages or helping to make you more successful
有利的；有優勢的；有好處的

example: The lower tax rate is particularly advantageous to poorer families.
低稅率對於較為貧困的家庭尤其有利。

NONE: › the fact of an event happening, an invention being made, or a person arriving
（事件、發明或人物的）出現，來臨，到來
› the period of four weeks before Christmas
降臨節；將臨期（聖誕節前的四個星期）

example: Life was transformed by the advent of the steam engine.
蒸汽機的出現使人類生活發生了翻天覆地的變化。

NONE: › a decorative piece of card, often hung on the wall, that has a small opening with a door for each of the days of the month before Christmas. Children open one of these doors each day, finding a picture under it.
基督降臨曆（掛在牆上的裝飾卡，上有小門，孩子在12月1日至聖誕節前每天打開一扇小門就可看到裡面的圖畫）
Seventh-Day Adventist
› not expected or planned
偶然的；非計劃中的

example: an adventitious event/situation
偶然事件／意外情況

NONE: A2 an unusual, exciting, and possibly dangerous activity, such as a trip or experience, or the excitement produced by such an activity
冒險，歷險；奇遇；刺激

example: She had some exciting adventures in Egypt.
她在埃及經歷了一些很刺激的奇遇。
We got lost on the Metro - it was quite an adventure.
我們在地鐵裡迷路了，還真是挺驚險的。
Sam won't come - he's got no sense of adventure (= he does not enjoy dangerous or exciting situations).
薩姆不會來的，他不喜歡冒險。

NONE: › a public open space where children can play and climb on structures, usually made of wood, ropes, and old tyres
（供兒童玩耍的）奇遇遊樂園，冒險樂園
› someone who enjoys and looks for dangerous and exciting experiences
冒險者；冒險家
› disapproving a person who takes risks, acts dishonestly, or uses the fact that they are sexually attractive to become rich or powerful
投機分子

example: He was something of an adventurer, living most of his life abroad.
他頗像個冒險家，一生大部分時間都是在國外度過的。
He was portrayed in the press as a gold digger and adventurer.
報紙把他描述成一個淘金者和投機分子。

NONE: B2 willing to try new or difficult things
喜歡冒險的；大膽創新的
› exciting and often dangerous
驚險刺激的，驚險的

example: I'm trying to be more adventurous with my cooking.
我正努力在烹飪方面有所創新。
She led an adventurous life.
她的一生充滿冒險刺激。

NONE: A2 a word that describes or gives more information about a verb, adjective, adverb, or phrase
副詞

example: In the phrase "she smiled cheerfully", the word "cheerfully" is an adverb.
在片語 she smiled cheerfully 中，cheerfully 是副詞。
In the phrase "the house was spotlessly clean", the word "spotlessly" is an adverb.
在片語 the house was spotlessly clean 中，spotlessly 是副詞。

NONE: › involving people opposing or disagreeing with each other
對立的；對抗的；敵對的

example: In the old days of two-party adversarial politics, voting was easy.
在過去兩黨對抗的政治環境中，決定投誰的票並不困難。

NONE: › an enemy
對手，敵手

example: He saw her as his main adversary within the company.
在他眼中，她是他在公司中的頭號對手。

NONE: C2 having a negative or harmful effect on something
不利的；負面的；有害的

example: The match has been cancelled because of adverse weather conditions.
由於天氣惡劣，這場比賽已被取消。
They received a lot of adverse publicity/criticism about the changes.
這些變化為他們招致種種負面報導／非議。
So far the drug is thought not to have any adverse effects.
迄今為止，人們一直認為這種藥物沒有任何副作用。

NONE: › a difficult or unlucky situation or event
逆境；不幸；厄運

example: She was always cheerful in adversity.
身處逆境時，她也從不垂頭喪氣。
The road to happiness is paved with adversities.
通往幸福的道路上荊棘滿途。

NONE: B1 an advertisement
一則廣告

example: an advert for the local radio station
當地廣播電臺推廣節目的廣告

NONE: B1 to make something known generally or in public, especially in order to sell it
（尤指為了推銷某物）登廣告，做廣告，宣傳；公佈；徵聘

example: We advertised our car in the local newspaper.
我們在當地報紙上登了廣告出售我們的轎車。
He advertises his services on the company notice board.
他在公司的佈告版上張貼廣告來宣傳其業務。
I'm going to advertise for (= put a notice in the newspaper, local shop, etc., asking for) someone to clean my house.
我打算登廣告僱個人來做家庭清潔。
There's no harm in applying for other jobs, but if I were you, I wouldn't advertise the fact (= make it generally known) at work.
去應徵其他的工作沒有害處。但如果是我的話，我就不會在上班時張揚這件事。

NONE: A2 informal ad, UK also informal advert a picture, short film, song, etc. that tries to persuade people to buy a product or service, or a piece of text that tells people about a job, etc.
廣告；啟事
› If you are an advertisement for something, you show its good effects.
現身說法宣傳…的好處；是…的活廣告

example: a television/newspaper advertisement for a new car
為一款新車做的電視／報紙廣告
She scanned the job/property advertisements in the paper.
她瀏覽了一下報紙的招聘／房地產廣告。
I'm afraid I'm not a very good advertisement for the diet since I've actually put on weight!
恐怕我不是這個減肥飲食計劃的活廣告，因為我的體重實際上是增加了！

NONE: B2 the business of trying to persuade people to buy products or services
廣告（業）

example: Fiona works in advertising.
菲奧納從事廣告業。
the advertising industry
廣告界

NONE: › an advertisement in a newspaper or magazine that is designed to look like an article by the writers of the magazine
社論式廣告
A2 an opinion that someone offers you about what you should do or how you should act in a particular situation
意見；忠告；勸告

example: Steven gave me some good advice.
斯蒂芬給了我一些好建議。
I think I'll take your advice (= do what you suggest) and get the green dress.
我想，我就聽你的建議，拿這件綠色連衣裙吧。
Can I give you a piece of advice?
你想聽聽我的建議嗎？
I need some advice on which computer to buy.
我需要聽聽別人的意見來決定買哪種電腦。
[ + to infinitive ] My advice is to go by train.
我建議坐火車去。
We went to Paris on Sarah's advice.
我們聽從薩拉的建議去了巴黎。

NONE: › If something is advisable, it will avoid problems if you do it.
明智的；可取的；適當的

example: [ + to infinitive ] It's advisable to book seats at least a week in advance.
最好至少提前一週預訂座位。
A certain amount of caution is advisable at this point.
此刻保持適度謹慎是明智的。

I or T: B1 [ I or T ] to give someone advice
勸告；忠告；向…提供意見，給…出主意

T: › [ T ] formal to give someone official information about something

example: [ + to infinitive ] I think I'd advise him to leave the company.
我想，我會建議他離開這家公司。
His doctor advised him against smoking.
他的醫生勸他戒煙。
I'd strongly advise against making a sudden decision.
我會極力奉勸不要草率作出決定。
[ + that ] They're advising that children be kept at home.
他們建議讓孩子們在家裡呆著。
[ + -ing verb ] I'd advise waiting until tomorrow.
我建議等到明天再說。
[ + question word ] She advised us when to come.
她給我們出主意，告訴我們該甚麼時候來。
She advises the president (= gives information and suggests types of action) on African policy.
她是總統的非洲政策顧問。
You would be well advised to (= it would be wise for you to) have the appropriate vaccinations before you go abroad.
明智的做法是，在出國前接種適當的疫苗。
They were advised of their rights.
他們獲悉自己的權利。
[ + that ] Our solicitors have advised that the costs could be enormous.
我們的律師已經告知我們，訴訟費用可能會非常高。

NONE: › If you say you are using a word advisedly, you mean you are choosing it after thinking about it very carefully.
深思熟慮地；經過認真思考

example: This action is barbaric - and I use the word advisedly.
這是野蠻的行為——我是經過深思熟慮才這樣說的。

NONE: › the process or activity of advising someone about something
勸告；建議；提供諮詢
› to consider something such as advice or information carefully
周密考慮…；對…深思熟慮

example: a counseling and advisement center
諮詢顧問中心
Contact Dr Gray about academic advisement.
學術問題諮詢，請聯絡格雷博士。
student/graduate/career advisement
學生／畢業生／職業指導
Thank you for your input Mr Walters - I'll take what you've said under advisement.
謝謝您不吝指教，沃爾特斯先生——我會仔細考慮您的意見的。

NONE: C1 someone whose job is to give advice about a subject
顧問

example: She is the party's main economic adviser.
她是該黨主要的經濟顧問。
a financial adviser
財政顧問

NONE: › giving advice
給予意見的
› an official announcement that contains advice, information, or a warning
報告；公告；警告

example: She is employed by the president in an advisory capacity.
她被總裁聘為顧問。
weather/travel advisories
天氣報告／旅遊公告
Television companies sometimes broadcast advisories before violent movies.
電視臺在播放有暴力內容的電影前，有時會先作警示。

NONE: C2 to publicly support or suggest an idea, development, or way of doing something
主張；擁護；支持；提倡

C: › a lawyer who defends someone in a law court
C2 someone who publicly supports something
主張人；擁護人；支持者；提倡者

example: [ + -ing verb ] She advocates taking a more long-term view.
她主張把目光放得更長遠一些。
He advocates the return of capital punishment.
他主張恢復死刑。
He's a strong advocate of state ownership of the railways.
他是鐵路國有的積極倡導人。
